name: Colistin (polymyxin E)
mechanism: Cationic detergent that disrupts bacterial cell membrane integrity (Gram-negative bacteria)
dosing: Dosing complex - use local guidance and consult pharmacy; typical IV dosing based on colistin base activity and renal function
interactions: Other nephrotoxic or neurotoxic agents (aminoglycosides, vancomycin, amphotericin)
monitoring: Renal function, respiratory status, neuromuscular blockade signs
pregnancy: Use only if no safer alternatives - limited data
sideEffects: Nephrotoxicity, neurotoxicity (paresthesia, dizziness, neuromuscular blockade), bronchospasm with inhaled forms
pharmacokinetics: Poor oral absorption; IV or inhaled administration. Renal clearance; dosing adjusted for renal impairment
clinicalPearls: Often used as a last-resort agent for multidrug-resistant Gram-negative infections; dosing regimens vary—consult infectious diseases/pharmacy
indication: Severe infections due to MDR Pseudomonas, Acinetobacter, Klebsiella species when other options exhausted
